source: Adapted from feat/parallel GPU-wrapper scheduling semantics without batch claiming or parallel worker launch.

modules.estimate_basis: DepthPro runs from a dedicated remote venv to avoid disturbing the hamer and ego_foundation environments. VRAM budget is conservative until wrapper/resource monitor observations are collected. The required V22 batch depth path remains UniDepth unless the run design enables this optional candidate.

Visible-surface lifting is CPU geometry, but it imports Open3D through build_v19_visible_geometry_from_sam2_depth.py; the remote ego_foundation environment has open3d while hamer does not.
OpenCV rendering and H.264 transcode are CPU-bound in current implementation.
Depth colorization uses NumPy/OpenCV and ffmpeg CPU encode.
Review overlay reads keyframe RGB, approved boxes, and SAM2 masks; no model inference.
Current observed mesh candidate uses accepted SAM2 masks plus selected depth backprojection, NumPy/OpenCV/trimesh, and no CUDA calls. This is not TRELLIS or neural mesh reconstruction.

Generic object mesh reconstruction is listed as CPU/GPU in the V22 harness. If the selected backend uses neural reconstruction, CUDA rasterization, diffusion, NeRF/SDF optimization, or learned completion, launch through the wrapper with this budget; pure geometry-only implementations may override to CPU with a recorded reason.

Scaled observed-mesh reconstruction can be pure depth/mask geometry or GPU-assisted. The runner must treat CUDA-enabled completion/refinement as GPU-heavy and use the wrapper; CPU-only depth carving remains CPU direct with explicit evidence.
Visual-hull/depth-carving is often CPU geometry, but GPU projection/rasterization backends need scheduled VRAM. Use this estimate when the implementation allocates CUDA tensors or GPU rasterizers.

TRELLIS-style generative mesh prior is remote GPU-heavy: image/condition encoders plus 3D latent diffusion/decoder and mesh extraction can occupy tens of GiB. Schedule on A800 with a conservative 40 GiB reservation unless measured logs justify lowering it.
Optional learned shape candidates, retrieval-refinement, or neural completion runners are GPU-heavy by default unless the selected backend is documented as CPU-only.
Current ICP/Umeyama rigid fit is NumPy CPU.
Current pose overlay samples mesh and projects with NumPy/OpenCV.
Current final renderer is OpenCV/trimesh projection plus CPU H.264 transcode; no CUDA model inference.
